_about: Labelled outcomes from end-to-end runs of the skill. One record per run that is
documented somewhere in this repo with enough detail to encode — task, the level
it should reach, and the trigger that justifies that level.
Why this file exists: the routing behaviour has already regressed once. Cold runs
3-4 gave the skill a compliance audit with no code in it and the skill did not fire
at all — every trigger in `description:` was a software noun. The fix was to the
description, not the method. `description:` is a single 1024-character field under
constant pressure to be shortened, so the same regression can recur silently on any
edit. `routing_terms` is the guard: those strings must survive in the description or
the request stops reaching the skill.
`provenance` says where the record came from: `author` and `cold` are runs that
happened, `unrun` is a documented path in SKILL.md that no logged run has exercised
yet. An `unrun` row guards the routing surface and nothing else — its expected_level
and trigger are the documented intent, never an observed result. Do not count them as
evidence, and overwrite the row the first time the path is actually run.
What check_routing.py can and cannot prove is stated in its docstring. Short version:
it verifies a request can still ROUTE IN. It cannot verify the skill then picks the
right level, because that needs a model. `expected_level` and `trigger` are recorded
for the human-run decision eval, and are asserted only for completeness.

fixtures.trigger: the work exceeds one context window — a week of raw reviews is ~240k tokens
fixtures.outcome: Fan out where forced (240k), rejoin where not (200 summaries = 30k). Published as the README's worked example.

routing_terms: I don't know what I've already covered

fixtures.trigger: the valid paths cannot be enumerated in advance — the route depends on what the work turns up, so the pre-ladder question in Phase 1 sends this to an agent harness rather than a level with a route table
fixtures.outcome: NO END-TO-END RUN YET. Recorded to guard the routing surface for the Phase 1 pre-ladder exit, which SKILL.md documents but no logged run has exercised. The level and trigger here are the documented intent, not an observed result — do not read this row as evidence the skill lands on level 2. Replace `provenance` with author or cold, and this text with what actually happened, the first time it is run.

_not_recorded: The README claims nine end-to-end runs. Six are written down in enough detail to
encode here; the rest were not recorded structurally at the time, which is precisely
why regression testing was not possible before now. Treat the gap as a finding, not
as a fixture set that is merely incomplete — and record new runs here as they happen.
